claims.text: At stage-3 ProductListScreen shows a StatusBanner with StatusTone.warning and the message savedListBanner ('Showing the saved list: the API did not answer, so it may be out of date.') when the loaded list is out of date.

ColorScheme is a set of colors based on the Material spec, the design system Flutter's built-in widgets follow; it has a fixed set of roles including error/onError, primary and surface with their 'on' partners, and no warning or success role.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API: ColorScheme class (class description, constructor parameters)

claims.text: A ThemeExtension is a Flutter class that adds a typed set of extra tokens to ThemeData, registered through ThemeData's extensions parameter.
claims.source_hint: content/glossary.yaml theme-extension; Flutter API: ThemeExtension, ThemeData.extensions

claims.text: Theme.of(context).extension<T>() returns the extension of type T registered in the ThemeData in force, typed as T?, and null when no extension of that type is registered.
A ThemeExtension subclass must implement copyWith and lerp (both abstract in ThemeExtension); lerp(other, t) takes a nullable other and a double t.

By default (themeAnimationStyle not noAnimation), when the theme changes MaterialApp animates from the old ThemeData to the new one (AnimatedTheme); ThemeData.lerp calls each extension's lerp at each step, and at the end the new theme is used as is.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API: MaterialApp.themeAnimationDuration, AnimatedTheme, ThemeData.lerp, Tween.transform

claims.text: At stage-3 StatusColors extends ThemeExtension<StatusColors> with four Color fields warning, onWarning, success, onSuccess; copyWith keeps each value not passed; lerp returns this when other is null, else Color.lerp per field.
At stage-3 buildTheme(brand, brightness) passes colorSchemeSeed, brightness and extensions: [brand.statusColors(brightness)]; main.dart calls it once for theme (light) and once for darkTheme (dark).

At stage-3 brand.dart, the only file allowed to write a raw color (no_raw_colors_test), holds lightStatus (warning 0xFF7A5900 with onWarning white) and darkStatus (warning 0xFFF5C451 with onWarning 0xFF3D2E00): a dark amber with white text in light, a light amber with dark text in dark.

At stage-3 StatusBanner takes a required tone (StatusTone: info, success, warning, error) that chooses its colors; _colors reads Theme.of(context).extension<StatusColors>()! before switching on the tone, for every tone; warning uses status.warning/onWarning.

With MaterialApp's default animated theme change, a lerp that returns this compiles but its colors do not blend and change in one step at the end of the theme change; a lerp left as throw UnimplementedError() throws during the change.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API: ThemeData.lerp (extensions), Tween.transform (t == 1.0 returns end); Dart: throw

claims.text: Dart's ! after a value asserts it is non-null and throws at run time when it is null. With no StatusColors registered, the ! in StatusBanner fails at build time, so every StatusBanner of any tone fails; this is not a compile error.

A color that must differ between light and dark belongs in the theme as an extension rather than in a constants file, because the theme picks the value once for every widget; constants suit values that never change with the theme.
